data.name: Breath
data.detailed_description:
What is the Breath?
The Breath is an experimental videogame for single player. Player act as a man, looking for something in the desert. Wandering, breathing, memory appeared, about her. He start imagine, and impatience won't let him rest. At the top of the dune, he saw a crystal tree. He can't tell. He is confused. Painful memory appear again, he remembered she is gone. But can't remember what he is doing. Unknowingly, he step on a crystal bridge. An exit door appeared. He is afraid and happy at the same time. But wound last night is still occupy.
Dazzling glare, frozen ground, weak breath, he remember that desperate morning which have no relative with her. The river of time never came back, only thing shows up is their past. More clear the memory is, more pain he will suffer. Untill he saw the emptiness. Huge doubt occupy his heart, what is real?
Nothing is real, except memory about her and every breath.

reviews.review:
[url=http://store.steampowered.com/curator/32482033/]Crim's Humble Opinion Curator[/url]

"Every deep thinker is more afraid of being understood than being misunderstood"

[b]the Breath[/b] is a sort of walking simulator combined with story telling potrayed through poetry. There isn't much being offered with this title. The scenery is nice and intriguing. The story or poetry if you so prefer to think of it as has potential to be an interesting thought provoker; however it is like the store page, not exactly translated well. Those who understand the language will be able to piece things together and understand it, but I imagine there is room for a better transition into english. I can not speak for the Chinese; but I imagine it is most likely the fluent language of the developer. 

Aside from walking in the mysterious landscapes and reading the poetry the player is given the option to breathe. As far as I can tell this does nothing but make you feel more immersed into the idea of needing to slow down and "Just Breathe". You click to hold your breath in; and when you let go you let your breath out. It adds to the immersion a bit and is an interesting component to the title.

The ending is really kind of it is what it is. This title will only take you 10-15 minutes to experience. In the last area you aren't led to believe it is over and you are left running around in an area where there are doors you previously were able to go through that you now are not able to. The only way to exit this area is by going to one of the corners of the map and finding a hole in the wall. You are not told anything else when going through this; instead it just restarts the game. Kind of a bad ending, since the player isn't really sure it is the end or not. 

[h1]Pros[/h1]
+Interesting scenery
+Somewhat thought provoking poetry
+Breathing adds immersion

[h1]Cons[/h1]
-English translation needs work
-Endpoint in game not clear
-Really short

This is a somewhat interesting experience but I can't honestly say I got much out of it. It is more of an art piece so it's a bit subjective in what you take away from it. I think the big thing that needs repaired with this title is the translation. It might be a better experience if translated better. For now I'd say pass on it. If there is a translation that smooths out the experience than maybe I'd say pick it up during a sale; but be aware there is not much to this title that can not be seen through a quick walkthrough video.
